explanation: Store each client’s credit minus a global offset. Updating all credits changes only the offset; lookup adds it back. Max scans the dictionary for the greatest normalized credit.
timeComplexity: Insert, Remove and Lookup: expected O(1); AddAll: O(1); Max: O(n), because this implementation scans all clients. The operation bounds reflect the displayed index: ordered set, randomized treap, or a Python scan for Max.
spaceComplexity: O(n) dictionary entries. The client dictionary and any ranking index contain one entry per live client.
attribution: Original Python implementation and reset-aware operation adapter independently authored for EPI Practice from its displayed contract and independently authored C# solution; no upstream reference source adapted.
correctness: For every client, stored+offset equals its current credit. Inserting replaces that stored value, removal deletes it, and AddAll changes every observable credit by the same amount. Since a common offset preserves comparisons, maximizing stored credit selects a valid maximum.
walkthrough: Insert client Nora with credit 4, then AddAll(6): Lookup(Nora) is 10. Reinsert Nora with credit 3, which replaces its absolute credit. Max is Nora; after removal Lookup is −1 and Max is empty. JSON arguments are [operations], with each operation [name,stringArg,intArg]. lookup/remove/max records carry expected observations, not extra callable parameters. Observed true means all operations validated.
edgeCases: The mathematical Max contract permits any maximum-credit client when credits tie; Python selects the first in dictionary iteration order.
Missing lookup returns −1 and missing removal returns false.
The judge maintains expected credits independently and accepts any existing client with the maximum credit. No universal tie-breaker is required.
